title: SQL settlement close with late revisions
initial_prompt: Read TASK.md. Establish the merchant settlement query on inputs/settlement.sqlite. Reconcile the initial processor export and keep your query and notes for later batches.

stages.message: Read TASK.md. Establish the merchant settlement query on inputs/settlement.sqlite. Reconcile the initial processor export and keep your query and notes for later batches.

The treasury export now contains cross-currency orders. Rates are fixed per order currency in fx; 10000 basis points means 1:1. Convert each per-order component with integer half-up rounding (x*rate+5000)//10000. Update your query and summarize which merchants changed.

The processor replay introduced revised events. Select only the highest revision of each event_id before status or amount filtering. A higher revision can void a previously settled capture. Preserve all earlier settlement rules.

Customer refunds have arrived. Per order, cap settled refunds at its settled captured amount before converting. The database is the complete cumulative snapshot. Update the query; retain zero-activity merchants.

Risk operations supplied chargebacks. Only posted chargebacks count, and each order’s chargeback debit is capped at capture minus the already-capped refund, in source cents. Convert the chargeback component separately. Keep all earlier behavior.

Complete the close on the final cumulative snapshot. Write output/reconciliation.csv using the required five columns, and leave solution/reconcile.sql runnable against this schema. Judge uses the final main snapshot and one small edge snapshot. Do not special-case IDs.
